clue.text: Somewhere in East London mother going back out to lunch

parts.note: Barking is a district of East London

indicators.note: going back tells us to read the word for mother from right to left

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A mother in an East End district heads back out for her lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns DAM into MAD; BARKING is a district in the London borough of Barking and Dagenham.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for being completely crazy or eccentric.

clue.text: Anxious state of feeble people after retirement

indicators.note: retirement suggests withdrawing backwards, so the word for feeble people is read in reverse

parts.note: wets are weak, ineffectual people, a British usage

explanation.surface: Feeble folk get anxious once they have retired from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after retirement' turns WETS round to give STEW; a 'wet' in British slang is a feeble, wishy-washy person.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being agitated or worried.

clue.text: Heard old name became fashionable

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone heard an old name that then came into vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' tempts a solver to look for a sound-alike, but here it just means caught, as in catching a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that caught on became popular, the idiom for a trend spreading.

clue.text: Label on outside of posh flipping sweet

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole assembled string over, so it is read backwards
outside of places the label-and-on pair around the letter for posh

parts.note: a tag is a label
taken as written
U stands for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A label is stuck on the outside of a smart, flipping expensive sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' makes the label-and-on pair wrap round U, and 'flipping' then reverses the lot, so 'sweet' is the confection, not 'posh flipping sweet' as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar, nuts and egg white, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Still drunk in hospital? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: in would normally put the drunk inside the hospital letter
this phrase flips the containment, so the hospital letter goes inside the drunk

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Is the patient still drunk while in hospital? No, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' tells you to put H inside SOT rather than SOT inside H.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, as is a shot.

clue.text: Shrewd criminals — one turned out to be patriotic

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or shrewd

indicators.note: turned out means expelled, so the letter for one is thrown out

parts.note: a thief is one criminal
I is the Roman numeral one
a lag is a convict, another criminal

explanation.surface: Of a gang of crafty crooks, one was ejected for being a patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminals' supplies two: THIEF and LAG; 'turned out' removes I from THIEF, leaving THEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying the flag is an idiom for showing support for your country.

clue.text: Elected bodies agitated about introduction of jail term for employee crime?

parts.note: a party elected is in power, so IN

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the jail initial
agitated suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order
introduction of points to the opening letter of the word jail

explanation.surface: Agitated elected representatives talk about jailing staff who steal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns BODIES into SIDEOB, and 'about' puts J (from 'introduction of jail') inside it to give SIDEJOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime committed by someone working within the targeted organisation is called this.

clue.text: Gamble involving one unknown composer

indicators.note: involving means surrounding, so the gamble goes round the other letters

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
I is the Roman numeral one
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A risky bet on a single unknown composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Bizet was the French composer of the opera Carmen.

clue.text: Carry on with second opportunity

parts.note: to cope is to manage, to carry on

explanation.surface: Someone told to carry on is given a second chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope is room or freedom to act, an opportunity.

clue.text: Diners reflected about drinks half-heartedly

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the word for about is reversed

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: half the heart goes: one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: sherries are drinks

explanation.surface: Diners thought about their drinks without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns ON into NO; 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Rs of SHERRIES. 'Diners' looks like the people eating, but means eating places.
explanation.definitionFit: A noshery is informal British slang for a restaurant or café, a diner.

clue.text: Angry with English county concealing origin of dreaded venomous creature

parts.note: black, as in a black mood, means angry

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the county holds the initial letter

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an English county

indicators.note: origin of points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An angry person in an English county hides from a feared poisonous animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island county off England's south coast, abbreviated IOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The black widow is a spider with a famously venomous bite.

clue.text: Programmes about screening a novel

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the concealed letters read backwards
screening means hiding behind, so the letters are concealed in the word

explanation.surface: TV programmes about the screening of a novel adaptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' conceals AMME in progrAMMEs, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel about the matchmaking Miss Woodhouse is titled Emma.

clue.text: Demand member of family stops within short time

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the relative fills the space between the other two pieces

parts.note: in means within
T is short for time
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A demand that a relative stop within a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly.

clue.text: Composition is endless work with poor score in a small group setting

indicators.note: endless removes the ends of the word work, keeping the centre
in places the poor score inside the small group
setting here means a mounting around the poor score

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
O, zero, is the poorest score

explanation.surface: A composition is never-ending work that scores badly when played in a small group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips both ends of work; 'in' and 'setting' put the zero inside the group, giving ATORIO. 'Composition' is the definition, with 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Shoot an advert

definitions.meaning: slang for firing a bullet into someone

explanation.definitionFit: Plug means to shoot someone in slang, and also a piece of publicity.

clue.text: Team given advantage in series of tests

parts.note: a football or cricket team has eleven players
a plus is an advantage

explanation.surface: A team is handed an edge in a series of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven-plus was an exam taken by British children at eleven to decide on grammar school places.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus was a group of exams sat by English pupils at about age eleven.

clue.text: Money bovver boys needed for shoes

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, money
skins are skinheads, the bovver boys of British slang for gangs looking for trouble

explanation.surface: Thugs need money for footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bovver boys were young British toughs, often skinheads, in heavy boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckskins are shoes made of soft deer or sheep leather.

clue.text: Strident American supporting firm after break-up oddly overlooked

indicators.note: after sends the even letters of break-up ahead of the firm, so they come first
in a down clue, supporting means placed under the previous piece
oddly overlooked means the odd letters are ignored, leaving the even ones

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A shrill American backs a company once its break-up has been largely ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly overlooked' leaves RAU from bReAkUp; 'after' and 'supporting' just set the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous means harsh and loud, which is strident.

clue.text: Informed folio will appear in new edition

indicators.note: will appear in places the folio letter inside the rearranged word
new suggests the letters of edition are made fresh in another order

explanation.surface: Readers are told a folio will feature in the next edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges EDITION into NOTIIED and F goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Notified means told or advised, so informed.

clue.text: Foremen do poorly being prepared to make easy profits

indicators.note: being prepared suggests the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Foremen who perform badly are getting ready to rake in easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'being prepared' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names money earned for little or no effort.

clue.text: Heroin hidden in run down boat

indicators.note: hidden in means placed inside, so the drug letter goes within

parts.note: dingy means shabby, run down
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Heroin is stashed in a shabby boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat.

clue.text: Is upset about hair style and ends in trouble far more drunk

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned letters surround the hairstyle
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a quiff is a tuft of hair brushed up at the front

indicators.note: ends in points to the final letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a hairstyle and ends up in far more trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IS into SI, which goes 'about' QUIFF; 'ends in' takes E and R from troublE faR.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk; this is its comparative.

clue.text: Film by a celebrity raised issue

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means written upwards, so the whole string reads backwards

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien
a name is a famous person

explanation.surface: A film by a big star brought up an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses ETANAME.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Striking politician in current drama

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
acting is drama
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician caught up in a current drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacting means hitting, so striking.

clue.text: People willing to check answer, wrong sort?

parts.note: a test is a check

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of sort are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: People are willing to check an answer and fear it is the wrong sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SORT into TORS. 'willing' looks like eager, but means making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Testators are people who make a will, so they are willing in that sense.

clue.text: In Oxford, say, was holding college's first exhibition

indicators.note: In placed first means the next pieces go inside the shoe

parts.note: an Oxford is a type of lace-up shoe

indicators.note: holding means containing, so was wraps around the college letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of college

explanation.surface: In Oxford, say, a college's first exhibition was held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university, but is a shoe; 'holding' puts C inside WAS to give WCAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a display or setting for exhibiting things.

clue.text: Dog that is left to protect a certain military commander

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so the remaining dog letters go round
left means departed, so the letters for that is go

parts.note: a collie is a dog
one means a certain, as in one Mr Smith

explanation.surface: A dog is left to guard a certain officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes IE from COLLIE, leaving COLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer commanding a regiment.

clue.text: Wrong marks repeatedly given in one examination

indicators.note: given in places the marks inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an oral is a spoken exam

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter is used twice

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Bad marks are handed out repeatedly in a single exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means morally wrong.

clue.text: Articles with points covering broad area

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means set on top of what follows

parts.note: S and W are compass points
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Articles with pointers cover a wide field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is a broad strip or area, of land or cut crop.
